Common Ground · Living Mapmaker

A living map woven by the people who move through a place. Built against the Loom of Legends reference drawings, one gauntlet wave at a time.

wave 5 · living-mapmaker.html — 2026-08-08 05:01 UTC — wave 5 of the loop

single largest remaining gap

Awaiting wave 6. The last two verdicts both landed on the landmark mark and on what accumulation does to the fabric over a year; both are closed and measured, and nothing has yet been said about the artifact in that state by anyone who did not build it.

Every gap on this board was found by a critic in fresh context driving the running artifact, never by reading code. The honest position after closing a wave is that the next gap is not yet known — the loop is what finds it.

Critic verdicts

Wave 1 five critics, fresh context

  • first touch The cold screen was empty and taught nothing; the ghost read as a GPS breadcrumb and left nothing behind. closed
  • map feel Pan inertia came from one untimed event and decayed per frame, so a careful drag threw the map 272 px and could not be stopped. closed
  • visual language Authorship used an eight-hue categorical palette, so a busy ground became a multi-series line chart. closed
  • weaving and return The weave came from polyline intersections, so it was driven by GPS jitter: 0 m of jitter produced nothing, 2 m produced a rope of landmark knots. closed
  • functional gauntlet All tabs on a device shared one identity: same-device sync was silently dead and two tabs minted the same op id for different strokes, losing work permanently. closed

Wave 2 four critics, fresh context

  • first touch The demonstration never actually crossed: the knot bloomed on a point the first thread came nowhere near. closed
  • visual language Threads were constant-width vector ribbons with a uniform casing and no interlacing, so the ground read as a flow diagram. partial
  • weaving and return Weight came to exactly three times the thread count whatever the number of people, so one person's habit drew identically to a shared commons. closed
  • functional gauntlet A single malformed op left a permanently black screen that survived reload. closed

Wave 3 two critics, fresh context

  • visual language The ground and the weave were two different drawings sharing a z-order: nothing in the ground was thread, nothing in the weave was ground. closed
  • integration Long-pressing the map to say a word opened the field and then destroyed it the instant you lifted your finger, so on a phone the whole tend/voice third of the product could not be used at all. closed
  • integration Any client could delete any other person's thread; an unpicked thread came home again on the next resync; the control kept beating forever once a peer arrived. closed
  • integration Two rotational arrows side by side meaning different things; graphite authors indistinguishable from roads; two of four fibre makes invisible; the ladder saturated so a place twelve people wore was drawn like one four people wore. closed

Wave 4 one critic, fresh context, living the whole proposition

  • over time Accumulation had no ceiling: thirty people over six months turned the map into an opaque wall of ribbon with no street, label, knot or person readable anywhere. closed
  • own finding Traces following real streets beaded a walked corridor into a rope of knots; a knot must be threads meeting at an angle, not threads sharing a road. closed
  • over time Eight fibres for thirty people meant every identity was shared about four ways. closed

Wave 5 two critics, fresh context

  • visual language The landmark field was a machine-regular cross-hatch inside a wireframe diamond, stamped identically everywhere — a decal on the map, not cloth. closed
  • whole proposition Across a year the fibre vanished and the knots became a tiled field of identical badges out-inking the threads forty to one, with every knot at the top of the ladder. closed
  • whole proposition Your own older thread rendered fainter than a newcomer's, so your own hand was the weakest thing on your screen; and knots drew fully formed before the threads that make them arrived. closed

Notes

Outbound internet is blocked in the build sandbox, so every screenshot here is the artifact in its offline state: the Atlanta geometry you see is real OpenStreetMap data compiled into the file itself, not raster tiles. On a phone with a network, tiles fade in underneath the ink and the map carries you anywhere.

Cross-device collaboration was verified against a real MQTT broker running locally, including late join, concurrent drawing, and reconnect convergence. In the wild the ground races three public brokers; if none answer, everything still works on the device and between its tabs.

The critics could not see the original reference drawings, which exist only in the conversation. They worked from a written reference brief describing each of the eight sheets.

Eleven pieces of dead code were removed in wave 3 on the integration critic's list: an unused constant that a comment still claimed was load-bearing, an event system with no listeners, an easing function nobody called, and a knot weight function only the test harness ever used.

Wave 4 was told to stop auditing subsystems and simply live the client's closing sentence in order, clause by clause. It broke on the last one, which is the one the whole thing exists for.
